title: Divine Providence and the Shelter of Truth
english: The manifest works of providence can serve as his face, for through them we perceive God; but his secret, private words are the basis of all things, though we do not perceive them in the perfection of reality.

From the disturbance of men—those human doctrines promising things to men while causing disturbance, through which they trouble the uninstructed—God, making those who hope in him outside of this disturbance, hides them in the secrecy of his face in all the ways mentioned. He will cover them in a tent from the opposition of tongues. He who has reached the perfection of all progress, having withdrawn from it, understands the truth through which it is un-deceivable; but he who encounters it while still progressing needs the covering of God in a tent, that is, of various tongues, or rather various false doctrines. For it is said toward the perfect: 'And every voice that shall rise up against you for judgment shall defeat them all' (Ps 30:22-23). For every heterodox word rises up desiring to be judged alongside the ecclesiastical opinion. But he who thinks the things of the church will defeat them all.

Not such a great wonder is worthy of being shown by the mercy of God in the hostile and smoothed-over cities, which would be wondered at if it occurred in a city of dominion; just as for this reason God is most blessed, being praised by those who have been rescued from greater disturbance. And the name of ecstasy signifies madness, and also denotes the wonder occurring with astonishment; the present word signifies the second of these meanings. For he says such a thing: 'In ecstasy,' that is, having occurred in astonishment, 'I have been cast away far from the presence of your eyes' (Ps 31:9), that is, far from the glory of your supervisory and inspecting powers; and since I have thus arranged, I pleaded not to remain cast away but that the face of [the Lord] might appear to me.

Ps 30:24: Since the truth that said 'I am the truth' (John 14:6) is one, many truths come to be in those who partake of the one, each soul having the truth, the type of which it received from the only-begotten truth.
Since, then, the Lord seeks out all these truths, he wishes to honor those who have them for these truths.
For this reason, his holy ones, seek him out, not without reward, resting upon the truth you have.
Ps 31:1a: And since the psalm has many hidden things, the one encountering it needs understanding, that he may be able to understand each of the things said obscurely.

Ps 31:1b-c: They say the difference between iniquities and sins is this: the sins of those who have not received any law at all are called iniquities, while those committed by transgression of the law are named sins.
Blessed, then, are those whose iniquities are forgiven, those now coming to the divine word; and blessed are those whose sins are covered, whenever, having disobeyed the law, they afterward repent.
For 'forgiveness' is said of iniquities, but 'covering' of sins, because iniquities are forgiven altogether.
For those who sin without law are pardonable; the hidden sins are not forgiven altogether but are overshadowed from love: 'For love covers a multitude of sins' (1 Pet 4:8).

And some apply the 'Blessed are they whose iniquities are forgiven' (Ps 31:1) to those who have received the bath unto forgiveness of sins, and the 'And whose sins are covered' to those who from repentance have covered their sins.
And there are those who take the first of the believing nations, and the second of those of the circumcision who have received the Savior.
Ps 31:2: The sinless one is called not simply a human being but a man, on account of perfection.
Thus, then, God does not reckon sin to him, either by forgiving it or by its not having happened at all.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
